authorization: User: etymologise all Indo-Aryan SIL surveys jointly; do everything; surface tough/unclear cases for audit once done.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 8376.1 *peṭṭa gives Hindi/Bengali peṭ and Oriya peṭa “belly”, distinct from poṭṭa and peḍḍuka. The survey pet spellings preserve the diagnostic e-vowel belly family, with the source’s dental-versus-retroflex transcription retained for audit rather than silently normalized in the data. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.

proposals.evidence: CDIAL 9153 barkara explicitly gives Hindi bakrī, Himalayan bākhro and bokrā under contamination with *bokka. Western bokaḍī requires distinguishing that expressive contamination and its retroflex extension; simple bokari/bakheri forms fit the named goat family. The comparative family link retains uncertainty about transfer between Indo-Aryan languages.
